_comment: DOM contract between the Chrome extension and each AI site, plus what each site is good at and how much of it a student gets for free (the router reads `strengths` and `free_tier` to decide who answers what). Served live at GET /api/extension/config, so when a site renames a button you edit THIS FILE and every installed extension picks it up on its next run — no re-install. Selector lists are tried in order, first match wins. VERIFY THESE against the live sites before launch.

routing._comment: Fallback map used when the routing AI is unavailable or its daily free allowance is spent. When it IS available it sorts the whole bank in one call and picks per question. A LIST value rotates questions of that type across the sites named — theory is the bulk of every bank and carries no file, so it is shared between sites with text headroom instead of piling on one. Graphs go to ChatGPT by the owner's decision. See _routing_evidence.

chatgpt.label: ChatGPT
chatgpt.strengths: best at numerical working and step-by-step math (leads math reasoning benchmarks), clean LaTeX, and reading/producing graphs — plots and curve questions go here. Fast, and the clearest explainer.
chatgpt.free_tier: unlimited text chat, but only 3 FILE UPLOADS PER DAY — so it is excellent for questions whose text is all you need, and nearly useless for questions that need the paper attached

claude.label: Claude
claude.strengths: best at long structured written answers, derivations, proofs and comparisons, and the strongest coder of the four (leads SWE-Bench Verified). Answers are the most complete and best organised — worth the most on a high-mark question.
claude.free_tier: the SMALLEST free allowance of the four — a compute pool that refills on 5-hour windows, around 15 messages in practice. Spend it on questions where depth earns marks, never on bulk. 5 file uploads per chat.

gemini.label: Gemini
gemini.strengths: best at diagrams and anything spatial — flowcharts, ER, architecture — and at reading figures out of an attached document; generous with file uploads, so it carries document mode.
gemini.free_tier: compute-pooled with 5-hour resets, and generous with files: 10 uploads per prompt at 100 MB each. Good headroom for questions that need the paper attached.

_upload_note: How long to wait after attaching a file before pressing send. A chat site rejects a send while an upload is still in flight, and a big question paper takes seconds.
_routing_evidence: Routing is set from measured strengths AND free-tier capacity (checked August 2026), across the three sites the product drives: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini. Kimi was tried as a fourth and dropped by the owner's decision after live testing. Capacity notes: ChatGPT free gives unlimited text chat but ~3 FILE UPLOADS/day, so document-mode questions lean on Gemini (10 uploads per prompt) first. Claude's free pool is the smallest (~15 messages per 5-hour window) and it is the strongest writer/coder, so it gets code and the high-mark structured answers, never the bulk. Graph questions go to ChatGPT per the owner's preference. Re-check free tiers before launch — they move every few months.
_document_sites_note: Ordered preference for a question answered by attaching the paper. Document mode uploads the file once per question, so upload headroom decides the order: Gemini (10 per prompt) first, Claude (5 per chat) next, ChatGPT (3 per DAY) last and only when nothing else is available.
